household.name: Marek & Ania
household.title: A Silesian Family Home
household.description: Family of four in an older detached house in Katowice with a heat pump. Marek works rotating shifts, Ania works hybrid, Kuba and Zosia go to school.

items: Marek works a 3-shift rota that rotates every week: morning (06–14, away 06–15), afternoon (14–22, away 14–23), night (22–06, away 22–07, sleeps 07–14). Mon–Fri, plus a Saturday shift on 1 in 4 weekends.
Ania works from home every Tuesday and Thursday and on 25% of the other weekdays; office days she is away 08–17.
Kuba (14) is at school 08–15 and Zosia (10) 08–14 on school days. Kuba has football Mon/Wed 16–18, Zosia dance Tue/Fri 16–18.
School breaks: 22–31 Dec, 2–15 Feb (Silesian winter break), 2–7 Apr (Easter), 27 Jun–31 Aug. Polish public holidays incl. 24 Dec (new since 2025).
Unplanned events the forecast cannot know: weekend family outings (35% of weekend days, 3–6 h), evenings out, sick days, occasional weekend trips.
Power and energy per use are drawn uniformly from the ranges in the brief (e.g. kettle 2 kW × 3–5 min, hob 1.5–3.5 kW).
Cooking follows meals: breakfast at each person's wake-up time, lunch when an adult is home, kids' snack after school, dinner 17:30–19:30 (± 45 min), and a late meal after Marek's shift.
Screens run only when their users are at home and awake; Ania's laptop runs through her home-office hours.
Washing machine ≈ 4.5 cycles/week, dishwasher ≈ 6 cycles/week, both started only when an adult is home.
Lighting is on when people are awake at home and the real solar radiation is below 20 W/m² (dark).
Air-to-water heat pump; older house heat loss 0.25 kW per °C (thermal). COP falls from 3.6 at 7 °C to 2.4 at −7 °C.

Setpoints 21 °C day, 19.5 °C night (22–06), 20 °C when nobody is home; heating fades out as the average outdoor temperature of the last 24 hours rises from 13 °C (full heating) to 17 °C (off), like a weather-compensated heat pump in spring and autumn.
Electric power 1.5–3.5 kW while running (brief); a smaller need means the heat pump cycles on and off within the hour.
Internal gains 80 W per person at home; solar gains from real radiation. No domestic hot water in the heat pump (not in the brief).
Real hourly weather for Katowice (50.26 °N, 19.02 °E) from Open-Meteo: archive for the history, forecast API for the next 7 days.
The historical profile is simulated hour by hour from the schedules above and the real weather, 1 Oct 2025 → yesterday (≈ 1 year, well above the 30-day minimum).
Times are local (Europe/Warsaw); on daylight-saving changes the missing or doubled hour is interpolated so every day has 24 hours.
HackoWatt common tariff €0.18 / €0.28 / €0.40 / €0.28 per kWh; export €0.08/kWh; PV €1,300 per kWp; PV running cost 1% of the investment per year.

PV production from JRC PVGIS for Katowice: south-facing, 35° tilt, 14% system loss, 2019–2023 hourly average → 1,072 kWh per kWp per year. Next-days PV from the Open-Meteo radiation forecast on the same tilted plane.
Payback = investment ÷ (yearly bill saving + export income − 1% running cost). Scenario B also moves the washing machine and dishwasher to the best hour of their window.
The forecast knows the planned calendar (shifts, home-office days, school, holidays) and the weather forecast — not the unplanned events.

8 models (incl. LSTM and GRU neural networks) are compared on 8 test weeks (winter, spring and the 4 latest weeks), each trained only on the data before its week; the most accurate one is used. It is calibrated so that at most 1 in 5 days is under-predicted, and a likely range (10–90 %) is shown.

Online learning: when smart-meter readings are available, every complete day is added to the history, the model is re-trained on all data and the calibration is refreshed (update_model.py). No real meter is connected in this demo.
The optimiser only moves the washing machine, the dishwasher and heat-pump timing (pre-heating the house before the €0.40 peak); comfort stays inside the chosen band.

insights.title: Heating is your biggest cost
insights.detail: 6,661 kWh of your 10,663 kWh a year goes to heating (≈ €1,865 of €3,202).
insights.tip: Small changes to heating matter more than anything else in the house.

insights.title: Every degree colder costs you
insights.detail: Each 1 °C drop in outdoor temperature adds about 2.5 kWh of heating per day (≈ €0.69).
insights.tip: Lowering the indoor setpoint by 1 °C saves roughly the same as a 1 °C warmer day.

insights.title: Today is a high-demand day
insights.detail: 18.4 kWh forecast vs 13.2 kWh on an average past day with similar weather (56 days at 14–18 °C). Heating today 5.6 kWh vs 2.6 kWh on those days — coldest hour 11.1 °C.
insights.tip: Follow today's actions: the plan pays off most on high-demand days.

insights.title: Your daily peak
insights.detail: Appliances add 1.42 kWh at 18:00 and 1.45 kWh at 19:00 on top of heating, at €0.40/kWh.
insights.tip: Avoid starting flexible appliances in these hours.

insights.title: The oven is a big occasional load
insights.detail: On days it is used it takes 1.9 kWh — 346 kWh a year (≈ €136).
insights.tip: Oven dinners in the 17–22 peak cost 43% more than before 17:00 — batch-cook at the weekend or use residual heat.

insights.title: Washing machine timing
insights.detail: 235 cycles a year (187 kWh), most often at 06:00. Running every cycle at the cheapest allowed hour saves about €28 a year.
insights.tip: Best price: €0.18/kWh (the cheapest hours of the day).

insights.title: Dishwasher timing
insights.detail: 309 cycles a year (312 kWh), most often at 20:00. Running every cycle at the cheapest allowed hour saves about €69 a year.
insights.tip: Best price: €0.18/kWh (the cheapest hours of the day).

insights.title: Heat-ahead over a year
insights.detail: Today's plan saves €0.23 on 6 kWh of heating. Applied to your 6,661 kWh of yearly heating that is roughly €275 (estimate).
insights.tip: Needs a heat-pump controller or smart thermostat that can follow a schedule.

insights.title: Always-on devices
insights.detail: Refrigerator, Wi-Fi router, Standby devices use 920 kWh a year, around the clock.
insights.tip: A switchable power strip removes part of the standby load.

insights.title: Marek's shift weeks
insights.detail: Without heating, weekdays in afternoon-shift weeks use 11.2 kWh and in morning-shift weeks 10.6 kWh (morning 10.6, afternoon 11.2, night 10.9). The forecast knows the rota in advance.
insights.tip: In night-shift weeks Marek sleeps 7–14 — quiet appliances (dishwasher, washer) are better started in the evening window or by timer.

insights.title: Ania's home-office days
insights.detail: Home-office weekdays use 11.2 kWh vs 10.7 kWh on office days (laptop, lunch cooking, kettle, lighting) — plus the house stays heated to 21 °C instead of 20 °C.
insights.tip: On home-office days, cook lunch and run the washing machine in the solar/cheaper midday hours instead of the evening.

insights.title: Short power peaks
insights.detail: In the evening the hour averages only 1.8 kWh, but for a few minutes hob, oven, kettle, dishwasher heater and heat pump run together: on 1 evening in 10 the power reaches 6.5 kW. Today's highest expected short peak: 7.1 kW around 08:00.
insights.tip: Stagger big loads: boil the kettle before the oven preheats, start the dishwasher after cooking (or by timer at night).

insights.title: The evening peak
insights.detail: 17:00–22:00 costs €0.40/kWh and is when the whole family is home (dinner, screens, heating): €1,310 of €3,202 a year.
insights.tip: Pre-heat before 17:00, start the dishwasher by timer after midnight, and use the oven before 17:00 on weekends.

household.name: Marek & Ania
household.title: A Silesian Family Home
household.description: Family of four in an older detached house in Katowice with a heat pump. Marek works rotating shifts, Ania works hybrid, Kuba and Zosia go to school.

items: Marek works a 3-shift rota that rotates every week: morning (06–14, away 06–15), afternoon (14–22, away 14–23), night (22–06, away 22–07, sleeps 07–14). Mon–Fri, plus a Saturday shift on 1 in 4 weekends.
Ania works from home every Tuesday and Thursday and on 25% of the other weekdays; office days she is away 08–17.
Kuba (14) is at school 08–15 and Zosia (10) 08–14 on school days. Kuba has football Mon/Wed 16–18, Zosia dance Tue/Fri 16–18.
School breaks: 22–31 Dec, 2–15 Feb (Silesian winter break), 2–7 Apr (Easter), 27 Jun–31 Aug. Polish public holidays incl. 24 Dec (new since 2025).
Unplanned events the forecast cannot know: weekend family outings (35% of weekend days, 3–6 h), evenings out, sick days, occasional weekend trips.
Power and energy per use are drawn uniformly from the ranges in the brief (e.g. kettle 2 kW × 3–5 min, hob 1.5–3.5 kW).
Cooking follows meals: breakfast at each person's wake-up time, lunch when an adult is home, kids' snack after school, dinner 17:30–19:30 (± 45 min), and a late meal after Marek's shift.
Screens run only when their users are at home and awake; Ania's laptop runs through her home-office hours.
Washing machine ≈ 4.5 cycles/week, dishwasher ≈ 6 cycles/week, both started only when an adult is home.
Lighting is on when people are awake at home and the real solar radiation is below 20 W/m² (dark).
Air-to-water heat pump; older house heat loss 0.25 kW per °C (thermal). COP falls from 3.6 at 7 °C to 2.4 at −7 °C.

Setpoints 21 °C day, 19.5 °C night (22–06), 20 °C when nobody is home; heating fades out as the average outdoor temperature of the last 24 hours rises from 13 °C (full heating) to 17 °C (off), like a weather-compensated heat pump in spring and autumn.
Electric power 1.5–3.5 kW while running (brief); a smaller need means the heat pump cycles on and off within the hour.
Internal gains 80 W per person at home; solar gains from real radiation. No domestic hot water in the heat pump (not in the brief).
Real hourly weather for Katowice (50.26 °N, 19.02 °E) from Open-Meteo: archive for the history, forecast API for the next 7 days.
The historical profile is simulated hour by hour from the schedules above and the real weather, 1 Oct 2025 → yesterday (≈ 1 year, well above the 30-day minimum).
Times are local (Europe/Warsaw); on daylight-saving changes the missing or doubled hour is interpolated so every day has 24 hours.
HackoWatt common tariff €0.18 / €0.28 / €0.40 / €0.28 per kWh; export €0.08/kWh; PV €1,300 per kWp; PV running cost 1% of the investment per year.

PV production from JRC PVGIS for Katowice: south-facing, 35° tilt, 14% system loss, 2019–2023 hourly average → 1,072 kWh per kWp per year. Next-days PV from the Open-Meteo radiation forecast on the same tilted plane.
Payback = investment ÷ (yearly bill saving + export income − 1% running cost). Scenario B also moves the washing machine and dishwasher to the best hour of their window.
The forecast knows the planned calendar (shifts, home-office days, school, holidays) and the weather forecast — not the unplanned events.

8 models (incl. LSTM and GRU neural networks) are compared on 8 test weeks (winter, spring and the 4 latest weeks), each trained only on the data before its week; the most accurate one is used. It is calibrated so that at most 1 in 5 days is under-predicted, and a likely range (10–90 %) is shown.

Online learning: when smart-meter readings are available, every complete day is added to the history, the model is re-trained on all data and the calibration is refreshed (update_model.py). No real meter is connected in this demo.
The optimiser only moves the washing machine, the dishwasher and heat-pump timing (pre-heating the house before the €0.40 peak); comfort stays inside the chosen band.

household.name: Marek & Ania
household.title: A Silesian Family Home
household.description: Family of four in an older detached house in Katowice with a heat pump. Marek works rotating shifts, Ania works hybrid, Kuba and Zosia go to school.

items: Marek works a 3-shift rota that rotates every week: morning (06–14, away 06–15), afternoon (14–22, away 14–23), night (22–06, away 22–07, sleeps 07–14). Mon–Fri, plus a Saturday shift on 1 in 4 weekends.
Ania works from home every Tuesday and Thursday and on 25% of the other weekdays; office days she is away 08–17.
Kuba (14) is at school 08–15 and Zosia (10) 08–14 on school days. Kuba has football Mon/Wed 16–18, Zosia dance Tue/Fri 16–18.
School breaks: 22–31 Dec, 2–15 Feb (Silesian winter break), 2–7 Apr (Easter), 27 Jun–31 Aug. Polish public holidays incl. 24 Dec (new since 2025).
Unplanned events the forecast cannot know: weekend family outings (35% of weekend days, 3–6 h), evenings out, sick days, occasional weekend trips.
Power and energy per use are drawn uniformly from the ranges in the brief (e.g. kettle 2 kW × 3–5 min, hob 1.5–3.5 kW).
Cooking follows meals: breakfast at each person's wake-up time, lunch when an adult is home, kids' snack after school, dinner 17:30–19:30 (± 45 min), and a late meal after Marek's shift.
Screens run only when their users are at home and awake; Ania's laptop runs through her home-office hours.
Washing machine ≈ 4.5 cycles/week, dishwasher ≈ 6 cycles/week, both started only when an adult is home.
Lighting is on when people are awake at home and the real solar radiation is below 20 W/m² (dark).
Air-to-water heat pump; older house heat loss 0.25 kW per °C (thermal). COP falls from 3.6 at 7 °C to 2.4 at −7 °C.

Setpoints 21 °C day, 19.5 °C night (22–06), 20 °C when nobody is home; heating fades out as the average outdoor temperature of the last 24 hours rises from 13 °C (full heating) to 17 °C (off), like a weather-compensated heat pump in spring and autumn.
Electric power 1.5–3.5 kW while running (brief); a smaller need means the heat pump cycles on and off within the hour.
Internal gains 80 W per person at home; solar gains from real radiation. No domestic hot water in the heat pump (not in the brief).
Real hourly weather for Katowice (50.26 °N, 19.02 °E) from Open-Meteo: archive for the history, forecast API for the next 7 days.
The historical profile is simulated hour by hour from the schedules above and the real weather, 1 Oct 2025 → yesterday (≈ 1 year, well above the 30-day minimum).
Times are local (Europe/Warsaw); on daylight-saving changes the missing or doubled hour is interpolated so every day has 24 hours.
HackoWatt common tariff €0.18 / €0.28 / €0.40 / €0.28 per kWh; export €0.08/kWh; PV €1,300 per kWp; PV running cost 1% of the investment per year.

PV production from JRC PVGIS for Katowice: south-facing, 35° tilt, 14% system loss, 2019–2023 hourly average → 1,072 kWh per kWp per year. Next-days PV from the Open-Meteo radiation forecast on the same tilted plane.
Payback = investment ÷ (yearly bill saving + export income − 1% running cost). Scenario B also moves the washing machine and dishwasher to the best hour of their window.
The forecast knows the planned calendar (shifts, home-office days, school, holidays) and the weather forecast — not the unplanned events.

8 models (incl. LSTM and GRU neural networks) are compared on 8 test weeks (winter, spring and the 4 latest weeks), each trained only on the data before its week; the most accurate one is used. It is calibrated so that at most 1 in 5 days is under-predicted, and a likely range (10–90 %) is shown.

Online learning: when smart-meter readings are available, every complete day is added to the history, the model is re-trained on all data and the calibration is refreshed (update_model.py). No real meter is connected in this demo.
The optimiser only moves the washing machine, the dishwasher and heat-pump timing (pre-heating the house before the €0.40 peak); comfort stays inside the chosen band.

insights.title: Heating is your biggest cost
insights.detail: 6,661 kWh of your 10,663 kWh a year goes to heating (≈ €1,865 of €3,202).
insights.tip: Small changes to heating matter more than anything else in the house.

insights.title: Every degree colder costs you
insights.detail: Each 1 °C drop in outdoor temperature adds about 2.5 kWh of heating per day (≈ €0.69).
insights.tip: Lowering the indoor setpoint by 1 °C saves roughly the same as a 1 °C warmer day.

insights.title: Today is a high-demand day
insights.detail: 18.4 kWh forecast vs 13.2 kWh on an average past day with similar weather (56 days at 14–18 °C). Heating today 5.6 kWh vs 2.6 kWh on those days — coldest hour 11.1 °C.
insights.tip: Follow today's actions: the plan pays off most on high-demand days.

insights.title: Your daily peak
insights.detail: Appliances add 1.42 kWh at 18:00 and 1.45 kWh at 19:00 on top of heating, at €0.40/kWh.
insights.tip: Avoid starting flexible appliances in these hours.

insights.title: The oven is a big occasional load
insights.detail: On days it is used it takes 1.9 kWh — 346 kWh a year (≈ €136).
insights.tip: Oven dinners in the 17–22 peak cost 43% more than before 17:00 — batch-cook at the weekend or use residual heat.

insights.title: Washing machine timing
insights.detail: 235 cycles a year (187 kWh), most often at 06:00. Running every cycle at the cheapest allowed hour saves about €28 a year.
insights.tip: Best price: €0.18/kWh (the cheapest hours of the day).

insights.title: Dishwasher timing
insights.detail: 309 cycles a year (312 kWh), most often at 20:00. Running every cycle at the cheapest allowed hour saves about €69 a year.
insights.tip: Best price: €0.18/kWh (the cheapest hours of the day).

insights.title: Heat-ahead over a year
insights.detail: Today's plan saves €0.61 on 6 kWh of heating. Applied to your 6,661 kWh of yearly heating that is roughly €728 (estimate).
insights.tip: Needs a heat-pump controller or smart thermostat that can follow a schedule.

insights.title: Always-on devices
insights.detail: Refrigerator, Wi-Fi router, Standby devices use 920 kWh a year, around the clock.
insights.tip: A switchable power strip removes part of the standby load.

insights.title: Marek's shift weeks
insights.detail: Without heating, weekdays in afternoon-shift weeks use 11.2 kWh and in morning-shift weeks 10.6 kWh (morning 10.6, afternoon 11.2, night 10.9). The forecast knows the rota in advance.
insights.tip: In night-shift weeks Marek sleeps 7–14 — quiet appliances (dishwasher, washer) are better started in the evening window or by timer.

insights.title: Ania's home-office days
insights.detail: Home-office weekdays use 11.2 kWh vs 10.7 kWh on office days (laptop, lunch cooking, kettle, lighting) — plus the house stays heated to 21 °C instead of 20 °C.
insights.tip: On home-office days, cook lunch and run the washing machine in the solar/cheaper midday hours instead of the evening.

insights.title: Short power peaks
insights.detail: In the evening the hour averages only 1.8 kWh, but for a few minutes hob, oven, kettle, dishwasher heater and heat pump run together: on 1 evening in 10 the power reaches 6.5 kW. Today's highest expected short peak: 7.1 kW around 08:00.
insights.tip: Stagger big loads: boil the kettle before the oven preheats, start the dishwasher after cooking (or by timer at night).

insights.title: The evening peak
insights.detail: 17:00–22:00 costs €0.40/kWh and is when the whole family is home (dinner, screens, heating): €1,310 of €3,202 a year.
insights.tip: Pre-heat before 17:00, start the dishwasher by timer after midnight, and use the oven before 17:00 on weekends.

household.name: Marek & Ania
household.title: A Silesian Family Home
household.description: Family of four in an older detached house in Katowice with a heat pump. Marek works rotating shifts, Ania works hybrid, Kuba and Zosia go to school.

items: Marek works a 3-shift rota that rotates every week: morning (06–14, away 06–15), afternoon (14–22, away 14–23), night (22–06, away 22–07, sleeps 07–14). Mon–Fri, plus a Saturday shift on 1 in 4 weekends.
Ania works from home every Tuesday and Thursday and on 25% of the other weekdays; office days she is away 08–17.
Kuba (14) is at school 08–15 and Zosia (10) 08–14 on school days. Kuba has football Mon/Wed 16–18, Zosia dance Tue/Fri 16–18.
School breaks: 22–31 Dec, 2–15 Feb (Silesian winter break), 2–7 Apr (Easter), 27 Jun–31 Aug. Polish public holidays incl. 24 Dec (new since 2025).
Unplanned events the forecast cannot know: weekend family outings (35% of weekend days, 3–6 h), evenings out, sick days, occasional weekend trips.
Power and energy per use are drawn uniformly from the ranges in the brief (e.g. kettle 2 kW × 3–5 min, hob 1.5–3.5 kW).
Cooking follows meals: breakfast at each person's wake-up time, lunch when an adult is home, kids' snack after school, dinner 17:30–19:30 (± 45 min), and a late meal after Marek's shift.
Screens run only when their users are at home and awake; Ania's laptop runs through her home-office hours.
Washing machine ≈ 4.5 cycles/week, dishwasher ≈ 6 cycles/week, both started only when an adult is home.
Lighting is on when people are awake at home and the real solar radiation is below 20 W/m² (dark).
Air-to-water heat pump; older house heat loss 0.25 kW per °C (thermal). COP falls from 3.6 at 7 °C to 2.4 at −7 °C.

Setpoints 21 °C day, 19.5 °C night (22–06), 20 °C when nobody is home; heating fades out as the average outdoor temperature of the last 24 hours rises from 13 °C (full heating) to 17 °C (off), like a weather-compensated heat pump in spring and autumn.
Electric power 1.5–3.5 kW while running (brief); a smaller need means the heat pump cycles on and off within the hour.
Internal gains 80 W per person at home; solar gains from real radiation. No domestic hot water in the heat pump (not in the brief).
Real hourly weather for Katowice (50.26 °N, 19.02 °E) from Open-Meteo: archive for the history, forecast API for the next 7 days.
The historical profile is simulated hour by hour from the schedules above and the real weather, 1 Oct 2025 → yesterday (≈ 1 year, well above the 30-day minimum).
Times are local (Europe/Warsaw); on daylight-saving changes the missing or doubled hour is interpolated so every day has 24 hours.
HackoWatt common tariff €0.18 / €0.28 / €0.40 / €0.28 per kWh; export €0.08/kWh; PV €1,300 per kWp; PV running cost 1% of the investment per year.

PV production from JRC PVGIS for Katowice: south-facing, 35° tilt, 14% system loss, 2019–2023 hourly average → 1,072 kWh per kWp per year. Next-days PV from the Open-Meteo radiation forecast on the same tilted plane.
Payback = investment ÷ (yearly bill saving + export income − 1% running cost). Scenario B also moves the washing machine and dishwasher to the best hour of their window.
The forecast knows the planned calendar (shifts, home-office days, school, holidays) and the weather forecast — not the unplanned events.

8 models (incl. LSTM and GRU neural networks) are compared on 8 test weeks (winter, spring and the 4 latest weeks), each trained only on the data before its week; the most accurate one is used. It is calibrated so that at most 1 in 5 days is under-predicted, and a likely range (10–90 %) is shown.

Online learning: when smart-meter readings are available, every complete day is added to the history, the model is re-trained on all data and the calibration is refreshed (update_model.py). No real meter is connected in this demo.
The optimiser only moves the washing machine, the dishwasher and heat-pump timing (pre-heating the house before the €0.40 peak); comfort stays inside the chosen band.

household.name: Marek & Ania
household.title: A Silesian Family Home
household.description: Family of four in an older detached house in Katowice with a heat pump. Marek works rotating shifts, Ania works hybrid, Kuba and Zosia go to school.

items: Marek works a 3-shift rota that rotates every week: morning (06–14, away 06–15), afternoon (14–22, away 14–23), night (22–06, away 22–07, sleeps 07–14). Mon–Fri, plus a Saturday shift on 1 in 4 weekends.
Ania works from home every Tuesday and Thursday and on 25% of the other weekdays; office days she is away 08–17.
Kuba (14) is at school 08–15 and Zosia (10) 08–14 on school days. Kuba has football Mon/Wed 16–18, Zosia dance Tue/Fri 16–18.
School breaks: 22–31 Dec, 2–15 Feb (Silesian winter break), 2–7 Apr (Easter), 27 Jun–31 Aug. Polish public holidays incl. 24 Dec (new since 2025).
Unplanned events the forecast cannot know: weekend family outings (35% of weekend days, 3–6 h), evenings out, sick days, occasional weekend trips.
Power and energy per use are drawn uniformly from the ranges in the brief (e.g. kettle 2 kW × 3–5 min, hob 1.5–3.5 kW).
Cooking follows meals: breakfast at each person's wake-up time, lunch when an adult is home, kids' snack after school, dinner 17:30–19:30 (± 45 min), and a late meal after Marek's shift.
Screens run only when their users are at home and awake; Ania's laptop runs through her home-office hours.
Washing machine ≈ 4.5 cycles/week, dishwasher ≈ 6 cycles/week, both started only when an adult is home.
Lighting is on when people are awake at home and the real solar radiation is below 20 W/m² (dark).
Air-to-water heat pump; older house heat loss 0.25 kW per °C (thermal). COP falls from 3.6 at 7 °C to 2.4 at −7 °C.

Setpoints 21 °C day, 19.5 °C night (22–06), 20 °C when nobody is home; heating fades out as the average outdoor temperature of the last 24 hours rises from 13 °C (full heating) to 17 °C (off), like a weather-compensated heat pump in spring and autumn.
Electric power 1.5–3.5 kW while running (brief); a smaller need means the heat pump cycles on and off within the hour.
Internal gains 80 W per person at home; solar gains from real radiation. No domestic hot water in the heat pump (not in the brief).
Real hourly weather for Katowice (50.26 °N, 19.02 °E) from Open-Meteo: archive for the history, forecast API for the next 7 days.
The historical profile is simulated hour by hour from the schedules above and the real weather, 1 Oct 2025 → yesterday (≈ 1 year, well above the 30-day minimum).
Times are local (Europe/Warsaw); on daylight-saving changes the missing or doubled hour is interpolated so every day has 24 hours.
HackoWatt common tariff €0.18 / €0.28 / €0.40 / €0.28 per kWh; export €0.08/kWh; PV €1,300 per kWp; PV running cost 1% of the investment per year.

PV production from JRC PVGIS for Katowice: south-facing, 35° tilt, 14% system loss, 2019–2023 hourly average → 1,072 kWh per kWp per year. Next-days PV from the Open-Meteo radiation forecast on the same tilted plane.
Payback = investment ÷ (yearly bill saving + export income − 1% running cost). Scenario B also moves the washing machine and dishwasher to the best hour of their window.
The forecast knows the planned calendar (shifts, home-office days, school, holidays) and the weather forecast — not the unplanned events.

8 models (incl. LSTM and GRU neural networks) are compared on 8 test weeks (winter, spring and the 4 latest weeks), each trained only on the data before its week; the most accurate one is used. It is calibrated so that at most 1 in 5 days is under-predicted, and a likely range (10–90 %) is shown.

Online learning: when smart-meter readings are available, every complete day is added to the history, the model is re-trained on all data and the calibration is refreshed (update_model.py). No real meter is connected in this demo.
The optimiser only moves the washing machine, the dishwasher and heat-pump timing (pre-heating the house before the €0.40 peak); comfort stays inside the chosen band.

insights.title: Heating is your biggest cost
insights.detail: 6,661 kWh of your 10,663 kWh a year goes to heating (≈ €1,865 of €3,202).
insights.tip: Small changes to heating matter more than anything else in the house.

insights.title: Every degree colder costs you
insights.detail: Each 1 °C drop in outdoor temperature adds about 2.5 kWh of heating per day (≈ €0.69).
insights.tip: Lowering the indoor setpoint by 1 °C saves roughly the same as a 1 °C warmer day.

insights.title: Today is a high-demand day
insights.detail: 18.4 kWh forecast vs 13.2 kWh on an average past day with similar weather (56 days at 14–18 °C). Heating today 5.6 kWh vs 2.6 kWh on those days — coldest hour 11.1 °C.
insights.tip: Follow today's actions: the plan pays off most on high-demand days.

insights.title: Your daily peak
insights.detail: Appliances add 1.42 kWh at 18:00 and 1.45 kWh at 19:00 on top of heating, at €0.40/kWh.
insights.tip: Avoid starting flexible appliances in these hours.

insights.title: The oven is a big occasional load
insights.detail: On days it is used it takes 1.9 kWh — 346 kWh a year (≈ €136).
insights.tip: Oven dinners in the 17–22 peak cost 43% more than before 17:00 — batch-cook at the weekend or use residual heat.

insights.title: Washing machine timing
insights.detail: 235 cycles a year (187 kWh), most often at 06:00. Running every cycle at the cheapest allowed hour saves about €28 a year.
insights.tip: Best price: €0.18/kWh (the cheapest hours of the day).

insights.title: Dishwasher timing
insights.detail: 309 cycles a year (312 kWh), most often at 20:00. Running every cycle at the cheapest allowed hour saves about €69 a year.
insights.tip: Best price: €0.18/kWh (the cheapest hours of the day).

insights.title: Heat-ahead over a year
insights.detail: Today's plan saves €0.23 on 6 kWh of heating. Applied to your 6,661 kWh of yearly heating that is roughly €275 (estimate).
insights.tip: Needs a heat-pump controller or smart thermostat that can follow a schedule.

insights.title: Always-on devices
insights.detail: Refrigerator, Wi-Fi router, Standby devices use 920 kWh a year, around the clock.
insights.tip: A switchable power strip removes part of the standby load.

insights.title: Marek's shift weeks
insights.detail: Without heating, weekdays in afternoon-shift weeks use 11.2 kWh and in morning-shift weeks 10.6 kWh (morning 10.6, afternoon 11.2, night 10.9). The forecast knows the rota in advance.
insights.tip: In night-shift weeks Marek sleeps 7–14 — quiet appliances (dishwasher, washer) are better started in the evening window or by timer.

insights.title: Ania's home-office days
insights.detail: Home-office weekdays use 11.2 kWh vs 10.7 kWh on office days (laptop, lunch cooking, kettle, lighting) — plus the house stays heated to 21 °C instead of 20 °C.
insights.tip: On home-office days, cook lunch and run the washing machine in the solar/cheaper midday hours instead of the evening.

insights.title: Short power peaks
insights.detail: In the evening the hour averages only 1.8 kWh, but for a few minutes hob, oven, kettle, dishwasher heater and heat pump run together: on 1 evening in 10 the power reaches 6.5 kW. Today's highest expected short peak: 7.1 kW around 08:00.
insights.tip: Stagger big loads: boil the kettle before the oven preheats, start the dishwasher after cooking (or by timer at night).

insights.title: The evening peak
insights.detail: 17:00–22:00 costs €0.40/kWh and is when the whole family is home (dinner, screens, heating): €1,310 of €3,202 a year.
insights.tip: Pre-heat before 17:00, start the dishwasher by timer after midnight, and use the oven before 17:00 on weekends.

household.name: Marek & Ania
household.title: A Silesian Family Home
household.description: Family of four in an older detached house in Katowice with a heat pump. Marek works rotating shifts, Ania works hybrid, Kuba and Zosia go to school.

items: Marek works a 3-shift rota that rotates every week: morning (06–14, away 06–15), afternoon (14–22, away 14–23), night (22–06, away 22–07, sleeps 07–14). Mon–Fri, plus a Saturday shift on 1 in 4 weekends.
Ania works from home every Tuesday and Thursday and on 25% of the other weekdays; office days she is away 08–17.
Kuba (14) is at school 08–15 and Zosia (10) 08–14 on school days. Kuba has football Mon/Wed 16–18, Zosia dance Tue/Fri 16–18.
School breaks: 22–31 Dec, 2–15 Feb (Silesian winter break), 2–7 Apr (Easter), 27 Jun–31 Aug. Polish public holidays incl. 24 Dec (new since 2025).
Unplanned events the forecast cannot know: weekend family outings (35% of weekend days, 3–6 h), evenings out, sick days, occasional weekend trips.
Power and energy per use are drawn uniformly from the ranges in the brief (e.g. kettle 2 kW × 3–5 min, hob 1.5–3.5 kW).
Cooking follows meals: breakfast at each person's wake-up time, lunch when an adult is home, kids' snack after school, dinner 17:30–19:30 (± 45 min), and a late meal after Marek's shift.
Screens run only when their users are at home and awake; Ania's laptop runs through her home-office hours.
Washing machine ≈ 4.5 cycles/week, dishwasher ≈ 6 cycles/week, both started only when an adult is home.
Lighting is on when people are awake at home and the real solar radiation is below 20 W/m² (dark).
Air-to-water heat pump; older house heat loss 0.25 kW per °C (thermal). COP falls from 3.6 at 7 °C to 2.4 at −7 °C.

Setpoints 21 °C day, 19.5 °C night (22–06), 20 °C when nobody is home; heating fades out as the average outdoor temperature of the last 24 hours rises from 13 °C (full heating) to 17 °C (off), like a weather-compensated heat pump in spring and autumn.
Electric power 1.5–3.5 kW while running (brief); a smaller need means the heat pump cycles on and off within the hour.
Internal gains 80 W per person at home; solar gains from real radiation. No domestic hot water in the heat pump (not in the brief).
Real hourly weather for Katowice (50.26 °N, 19.02 °E) from Open-Meteo: archive for the history, forecast API for the next 7 days.
The historical profile is simulated hour by hour from the schedules above and the real weather, 1 Oct 2025 → yesterday (≈ 1 year, well above the 30-day minimum).
Times are local (Europe/Warsaw); on daylight-saving changes the missing or doubled hour is interpolated so every day has 24 hours.
HackoWatt common tariff €0.18 / €0.28 / €0.40 / €0.28 per kWh; export €0.08/kWh; PV €1,300 per kWp; PV running cost 1% of the investment per year.

PV production from JRC PVGIS for Katowice: south-facing, 35° tilt, 14% system loss, 2019–2023 hourly average → 1,072 kWh per kWp per year. Next-days PV from the Open-Meteo radiation forecast on the same tilted plane.
Payback = investment ÷ (yearly bill saving + export income − 1% running cost). Scenario B also moves the washing machine and dishwasher to the best hour of their window.
The forecast knows the planned calendar (shifts, home-office days, school, holidays) and the weather forecast — not the unplanned events.

8 models (incl. LSTM and GRU neural networks) are compared on 8 test weeks (winter, spring and the 4 latest weeks), each trained only on the data before its week; the most accurate one is used. It is calibrated so that at most 1 in 5 days is under-predicted, and a likely range (10–90 %) is shown.

Online learning: when smart-meter readings are available, every complete day is added to the history, the model is re-trained on all data and the calibration is refreshed (update_model.py). No real meter is connected in this demo.
The optimiser only moves the washing machine, the dishwasher and heat-pump timing (pre-heating the house before the €0.40 peak); comfort stays inside the chosen band.

household.name: Marek & Ania
household.title: A Silesian Family Home
household.description: Family of four in an older detached house in Katowice with a heat pump. Marek works rotating shifts, Ania works hybrid, Kuba and Zosia go to school.

items: Marek works a 3-shift rota that rotates every week: morning (06–14, away 06–15), afternoon (14–22, away 14–23), night (22–06, away 22–07, sleeps 07–14). Mon–Fri, plus a Saturday shift on 1 in 4 weekends.
Ania works from home every Tuesday and Thursday and on 25% of the other weekdays; office days she is away 08–17.
Kuba (14) is at school 08–15 and Zosia (10) 08–14 on school days. Kuba has football Mon/Wed 16–18, Zosia dance Tue/Fri 16–18.
School breaks: 22–31 Dec, 2–15 Feb (Silesian winter break), 2–7 Apr (Easter), 27 Jun–31 Aug. Polish public holidays incl. 24 Dec (new since 2025).
Unplanned events the forecast cannot know: weekend family outings (35% of weekend days, 3–6 h), evenings out, sick days, occasional weekend trips.
Power and energy per use are drawn uniformly from the ranges in the brief (e.g. kettle 2 kW × 3–5 min, hob 1.5–3.5 kW).
Cooking follows meals: breakfast at each person's wake-up time, lunch when an adult is home, kids' snack after school, dinner 17:30–19:30 (± 45 min), and a late meal after Marek's shift.
Screens run only when their users are at home and awake; Ania's laptop runs through her home-office hours.
Washing machine ≈ 4.5 cycles/week, dishwasher ≈ 6 cycles/week, both started only when an adult is home.
Lighting is on when people are awake at home and the real solar radiation is below 20 W/m² (dark).
Air-to-water heat pump; older house heat loss 0.25 kW per °C (thermal). COP falls from 3.6 at 7 °C to 2.4 at −7 °C.

Setpoints 21 °C day, 19.5 °C night (22–06), 20 °C when nobody is home; heating fades out as the average outdoor temperature of the last 24 hours rises from 13 °C (full heating) to 17 °C (off), like a weather-compensated heat pump in spring and autumn.
Electric power 1.5–3.5 kW while running (brief); a smaller need means the heat pump cycles on and off within the hour.
Internal gains 80 W per person at home; solar gains from real radiation. No domestic hot water in the heat pump (not in the brief).
Real hourly weather for Katowice (50.26 °N, 19.02 °E) from Open-Meteo: archive for the history, forecast API for the next 7 days.
The historical profile is simulated hour by hour from the schedules above and the real weather, 1 Oct 2025 → yesterday (≈ 1 year, well above the 30-day minimum).
Times are local (Europe/Warsaw); on daylight-saving changes the missing or doubled hour is interpolated so every day has 24 hours.
HackoWatt common tariff €0.18 / €0.28 / €0.40 / €0.28 per kWh; export €0.08/kWh; PV €1,300 per kWp; PV running cost 1% of the investment per year.

PV production from JRC PVGIS for Katowice: south-facing, 35° tilt, 14% system loss, 2019–2023 hourly average → 1,072 kWh per kWp per year. Next-days PV from the Open-Meteo radiation forecast on the same tilted plane.
Payback = investment ÷ (yearly bill saving + export income − 1% running cost). Scenario B also moves the washing machine and dishwasher to the best hour of their window.
The forecast knows the planned calendar (shifts, home-office days, school, holidays) and the weather forecast — not the unplanned events.

8 models (incl. LSTM and GRU neural networks) are compared on 8 test weeks (winter, spring and the 4 latest weeks), each trained only on the data before its week; the most accurate one is used. It is calibrated so that at most 1 in 5 days is under-predicted, and a likely range (10–90 %) is shown.

Online learning: when smart-meter readings are available, every complete day is added to the history, the model is re-trained on all data and the calibration is refreshed (update_model.py). No real meter is connected in this demo.
The optimiser only moves the washing machine, the dishwasher and heat-pump timing (pre-heating the house before the €0.40 peak); comfort stays inside the chosen band.

insights.title: Heating is your biggest cost
insights.detail: 6,661 kWh of your 10,663 kWh a year goes to heating (≈ €1,865 of €3,202).
insights.tip: Small changes to heating matter more than anything else in the house.

insights.title: Every degree colder costs you
insights.detail: Each 1 °C drop in outdoor temperature adds about 2.5 kWh of heating per day (≈ €0.69).
insights.tip: Lowering the indoor setpoint by 1 °C saves roughly the same as a 1 °C warmer day.

insights.title: Today is a high-demand day
insights.detail: 18.4 kWh forecast vs 13.2 kWh on an average past day with similar weather (56 days at 14–18 °C). Heating today 5.6 kWh vs 2.6 kWh on those days — coldest hour 11.1 °C.
insights.tip: Follow today's actions: the plan pays off most on high-demand days.

insights.title: Your daily peak
insights.detail: Appliances add 1.42 kWh at 18:00 and 1.45 kWh at 19:00 on top of heating, at €0.40/kWh.
insights.tip: Avoid starting flexible appliances in these hours.

insights.title: The oven is a big occasional load
insights.detail: On days it is used it takes 1.9 kWh — 346 kWh a year (≈ €136).
insights.tip: Oven dinners in the 17–22 peak cost 43% more than before 17:00 — batch-cook at the weekend or use residual heat.

insights.title: Washing machine timing
insights.detail: 235 cycles a year (187 kWh), most often at 06:00. Running every cycle at the cheapest allowed hour saves about €28 a year.
insights.tip: Best price: €0.18/kWh (the cheapest hours of the day).

insights.title: Dishwasher timing
insights.detail: 309 cycles a year (312 kWh), most often at 20:00. Running every cycle at the cheapest allowed hour saves about €69 a year.

insights.title: Heat-ahead over a year

insights.tip: Needs a heat-pump controller or smart thermostat that can follow a schedule.

insights.title: Heating is your biggest cost
insights.detail: 6,661 kWh of your 10,663 kWh a year goes to heating (≈ €1,865 of €3,202).
insights.tip: Small changes to heating matter more than anything else in the house.

insights.title: Every degree colder costs you
insights.detail: Each 1 °C drop in outdoor temperature adds about 2.5 kWh of heating per day (≈ €0.69).
insights.tip: Lowering the indoor setpoint by 1 °C saves roughly the same as a 1 °C warmer day.

insights.title: Today is a high-demand day
insights.detail: 18.4 kWh forecast vs 13.2 kWh on an average past day with similar weather (56 days at 14–18 °C). Heating today 5.6 kWh vs 2.6 kWh on those days — coldest hour 11.1 °C.
insights.tip: Follow today's actions: the plan pays off most on high-demand days.

insights.title: Your daily peak
insights.detail: Appliances add 1.42 kWh at 18:00 and 1.45 kWh at 19:00 on top of heating, at €0.40/kWh.
insights.tip: Avoid starting flexible appliances in these hours.

insights.title: The oven is a big occasional load
insights.detail: On days it is used it takes 1.9 kWh — 346 kWh a year (≈ €136).
insights.tip: Oven dinners in the 17–22 peak cost 43% more than before 17:00 — batch-cook at the weekend or use residual heat.

insights.title: Washing machine timing
insights.detail: 235 cycles a year (187 kWh), most often at 06:00. Running every cycle at the cheapest allowed hour saves about €28 a year.
insights.tip: Best price: €0.18/kWh (the cheapest hours of the day).

insights.title: Dishwasher timing
insights.detail: 309 cycles a year (312 kWh), most often at 20:00. Running every cycle at the cheapest allowed hour saves about €69 a year.
insights.tip: Best price: €0.18/kWh (the cheapest hours of the day).

insights.title: Heat-ahead over a year
insights.detail: Today's plan saves €0.21 on 6 kWh of heating. Applied to your 6,661 kWh of yearly heating that is roughly €251 (estimate).
insights.tip: Needs a heat-pump controller or smart thermostat that can follow a schedule.

insights.title: Always-on devices
insights.detail: Refrigerator, Wi-Fi router, Standby devices use 920 kWh a year, around the clock.
insights.tip: A switchable power strip removes part of the standby load.

insights.title: Marek's shift weeks
insights.detail: Without heating, weekdays in afternoon-shift weeks use 11.2 kWh and in morning-shift weeks 10.6 kWh (morning 10.6, afternoon 11.2, night 10.9). The forecast knows the rota in advance.
insights.tip: In night-shift weeks Marek sleeps 7–14 — quiet appliances (dishwasher, washer) are better started in the evening window or by timer.

insights.title: Ania's home-office days
insights.detail: Home-office weekdays use 11.2 kWh vs 10.7 kWh on office days (laptop, lunch cooking, kettle, lighting) — plus the house stays heated to 21 °C instead of 20 °C.
insights.tip: On home-office days, cook lunch and run the washing machine in the solar/cheaper midday hours instead of the evening.

insights.title: Short power peaks
insights.detail: In the evening the hour averages only 1.8 kWh, but for a few minutes hob, oven, kettle, dishwasher heater and heat pump run together: on 1 evening in 10 the power reaches 6.5 kW. Today's highest expected short peak: 7.1 kW around 08:00.
insights.tip: Stagger big loads: boil the kettle before the oven preheats, start the dishwasher after cooking (or by timer at night).

insights.title: The evening peak
insights.detail: 17:00–22:00 costs €0.40/kWh and is when the whole family is home (dinner, screens, heating): €1,310 of €3,202 a year.
insights.tip: Pre-heat before 17:00, start the dishwasher by timer after midnight, and use the oven before 17:00 on weekends.

household.name: Marek & Ania
household.title: A Silesian Family Home
household.description: Family of four in an older detached house in Katowice with a heat pump. Marek works rotating shifts, Ania works hybrid, Kuba and Zosia go to school.

items: Marek works a 3-shift rota that rotates every week: morning (06–14, away 06–15), afternoon (14–22, away 14–23), night (22–06, away 22–07, sleeps 07–14). Mon–Fri, plus a Saturday shift on 1 in 4 weekends.
Ania works from home every Tuesday and Thursday and on 25% of the other weekdays; office days she is away 08–17.
Kuba (14) is at school 08–15 and Zosia (10) 08–14 on school days. Kuba has football Mon/Wed 16–18, Zosia dance Tue/Fri 16–18.
School breaks: 22–31 Dec, 2–15 Feb (Silesian winter break), 2–7 Apr (Easter), 27 Jun–31 Aug. Polish public holidays incl. 24 Dec (new since 2025).
Unplanned events the forecast cannot know: weekend family outings (35% of weekend days, 3–6 h), evenings out, sick days, occasional weekend trips.
Power and energy per use are drawn uniformly from the ranges in the brief (e.g. kettle 2 kW × 3–5 min, hob 1.5–3.5 kW).
Cooking follows meals: breakfast at each person's wake-up time, lunch when an adult is home, kids' snack after school, dinner 17:30–19:30 (± 45 min), and a late meal after Marek's shift.
Screens run only when their users are at home and awake; Ania's laptop runs through her home-office hours.
Washing machine ≈ 4.5 cycles/week, dishwasher ≈ 6 cycles/week, both started only when an adult is home.
Lighting is on when people are awake at home and the real solar radiation is below 20 W/m² (dark).
Air-to-water heat pump; older house heat loss 0.25 kW per °C (thermal). COP falls from 3.6 at 7 °C to 2.4 at −7 °C.

Setpoints 21 °C day, 19.5 °C night (22–06), 20 °C when nobody is home; heating fades out as the average outdoor temperature of the last 24 hours rises from 13 °C (full heating) to 17 °C (off), like a weather-compensated heat pump in spring and autumn.
Electric power 1.5–3.5 kW while running (brief); a smaller need means the heat pump cycles on and off within the hour.
Internal gains 80 W per person at home; solar gains from real radiation. No domestic hot water in the heat pump (not in the brief).
Real hourly weather for Katowice (50.26 °N, 19.02 °E) from Open-Meteo: archive for the history, forecast API for the next 7 days.
The historical profile is simulated hour by hour from the schedules above and the real weather, 1 Oct 2025 → yesterday (≈ 1 year, well above the 30-day minimum).
Times are local (Europe/Warsaw); on daylight-saving changes the missing or doubled hour is interpolated so every day has 24 hours.
HackoWatt common tariff €0.18 / €0.28 / €0.40 / €0.28 per kWh; export €0.08/kWh; PV €1,300 per kWp; PV running cost 1% of the investment per year.

PV production from JRC PVGIS for Katowice: south-facing, 35° tilt, 14% system loss, 2019–2023 hourly average → 1,072 kWh per kWp per year. Next-days PV from the Open-Meteo radiation forecast on the same tilted plane.

insights.title: Your daily peak

household.name: Marek & Ania
household.title: A Silesian Family Home
household.description: Family of four in an older detached house in Katowice with a heat pump. Marek works rotating shifts, Ania works hybrid, Kuba and Zosia go to school.

items: Marek works a 3-shift rota that rotates every week: morning (06–14, away 06–15), afternoon (14–22, away 14–23), night (22–06, away 22–07, sleeps 07–14). Mon–Fri, plus a Saturday shift on 1 in 4 weekends.
Ania works from home every Tuesday and Thursday and on 25% of the other weekdays; office days she is away 08–17.
Kuba (14) is at school 08–15 and Zosia (10) 08–14 on school days. Kuba has football Mon/Wed 16–18, Zosia dance Tue/Fri 16–18.
School breaks: 22–31 Dec, 2–15 Feb (Silesian winter break), 2–7 Apr (Easter), 27 Jun–31 Aug. Polish public holidays incl. 24 Dec (new since 2025).
Unplanned events the forecast cannot know: weekend family outings (35% of weekend days, 3–6 h), evenings out, sick days, occasional weekend trips.
Power and energy per use are drawn uniformly from the ranges in the brief (e.g. kettle 2 kW × 3–5 min, hob 1.5–3.5 kW).
Cooking follows meals: breakfast at each person's wake-up time, lunch when an adult is home, kids' snack after school, dinner 17:30–19:30 (± 45 min), and a late meal after Marek's shift.
Screens run only when their users are at home and awake; Ania's laptop runs through her home-office hours.
Washing machine ≈ 4.5 cycles/week, dishwasher ≈ 6 cycles/week, both started only when an adult is home.
Lighting is on when people are awake at home and the real solar radiation is below 20 W/m² (dark).
Air-to-water heat pump; older house heat loss 0.25 kW per °C (thermal). COP falls from 3.6 at 7 °C to 2.4 at −7 °C.

Setpoints 21 °C day, 19.5 °C night (22–06), 20 °C when nobody is home; heating fades out as the average outdoor temperature of the last 24 hours rises from 13 °C (full heating) to 17 °C (off), like a weather-compensated heat pump in spring and autumn.
Electric power 1.5–3.5 kW while running (brief); a smaller need means the heat pump cycles on and off within the hour.
Internal gains 80 W per person at home; solar gains from real radiation. No domestic hot water in the heat pump (not in the brief).
Real hourly weather for Katowice (50.26 °N, 19.02 °E) from Open-Meteo: archive for the history, forecast API for the next 7 days.
The historical profile is simulated hour by hour from the schedules above and the real weather, 1 Oct 2025 → yesterday (≈ 1 year, well above the 30-day minimum).
Times are local (Europe/Warsaw); on daylight-saving changes the missing or doubled hour is interpolated so every day has 24 hours.
HackoWatt common tariff €0.18 / €0.28 / €0.40 / €0.28 per kWh; export €0.08/kWh; PV €1,300 per kWp; PV running cost 1% of the investment per year.

PV production from JRC PVGIS for Katowice: south-facing, 35° tilt, 14% system loss, 2019–2023 hourly average → 1,072 kWh per kWp per year. Next-days PV from the Open-Meteo radiation forecast on the same tilted plane.
Payback = investment ÷ (yearly bill saving + export income − 1% running cost). Scenario B also moves the washing machine and dishwasher to the best hour of their window.
The forecast knows the planned calendar (shifts, home-office days, school, holidays) and the weather forecast — not the unplanned events.

8 models (incl. LSTM and GRU neural networks) are compared on 8 test weeks (winter, spring and the 4 latest weeks), each trained only on the data before its week; the most accurate one is used. It is calibrated so that at most 1 in 5 days is under-predicted, and a likely range (10–90 %) is shown.

Online learning: when smart-meter readings are available, every complete day is added to the history, the model is re-trained on all data and the calibration is refreshed (update_model.py). No real meter is connected in this demo.
The optimiser only moves the washing machine, the dishwasher and heat-pump timing (pre-heating the house before the €0.40 peak); comfort stays inside the chosen band.

insights.title: Heating is your biggest cost
insights.detail: 6,661 kWh of your 10,663 kWh a year goes to heating (≈ €1,865 of €3,202).
insights.tip: Small changes to heating matter more than anything else in the house.

insights.title: Every degree colder costs you
insights.detail: Each 1 °C drop in outdoor temperature adds about 2.5 kWh of heating per day (≈ €0.69).
insights.tip: Lowering the indoor setpoint by 1 °C saves roughly the same as a 1 °C warmer day.

insights.title: Today is a high-demand day
insights.detail: 18.4 kWh forecast vs 13.2 kWh on an average past day with similar weather (56 days at 14–18 °C). Heating today 5.6 kWh vs 2.6 kWh on those days — coldest hour 11.1 °C.
insights.tip: Follow today's actions: the plan pays off most on high-demand days.

insights.title: Your daily peak
insights.detail: Appliances add 1.42 kWh at 18:00 and 1.45 kWh at 19:00 on top of heating, at €0.40/kWh.
insights.tip: Avoid starting flexible appliances in these hours.

insights.title: The oven is a big occasional load
insights.detail: On days it is used it takes 1.9 kWh — 346 kWh a year (≈ €136).
insights.tip: Oven dinners in the 17–22 peak cost 43% more than before 17:00 — batch-cook at the weekend or use residual heat.

insights.title: Washing machine timing
insights.detail: 235 cycles a year (187 kWh), most often at 06:00. Running every cycle at the cheapest allowed hour saves about €28 a year.
insights.tip: Best price: €0.18/kWh (the cheapest hours of the day).

insights.title: Dishwasher timing
insights.detail: 309 cycles a year (312 kWh), most often at 20:00. Running every cycle at the cheapest allowed hour saves about €69 a year.
insights.tip: Best price: €0.18/kWh (the cheapest hours of the day).

insights.title: Heat-ahead over a year
insights.detail: Today's plan saves €0.23 on 6 kWh of heating. Applied to your 6,661 kWh of yearly heating that is roughly €275 (estimate).
insights.tip: Needs a heat-pump controller or smart thermostat that can follow a schedule.

insights.title: Always-on devices
insights.detail: Refrigerator, Wi-Fi router, Standby devices use 920 kWh a year, around the clock.
insights.tip: A switchable power strip removes part of the standby load.

insights.title: Marek's shift weeks
insights.detail: Without heating, weekdays in afternoon-shift weeks use 11.2 kWh and in morning-shift weeks 10.6 kWh (morning 10.6, afternoon 11.2, night 10.9). The forecast knows the rota in advance.
insights.tip: In night-shift weeks Marek sleeps 7–14 — quiet appliances (dishwasher, washer) are better started in the evening window or by timer.

insights.title: Ania's home-office days
insights.detail: Home-office weekdays use 11.2 kWh vs 10.7 kWh on office days (laptop, lunch cooking, kettle, lighting) — plus the house stays heated to 21 °C instead of 20 °C.
insights.tip: On home-office days, cook lunch and run the washing machine in the solar/cheaper midday hours instead of the evening.

insights.title: Short power peaks
insights.detail: In the evening the hour averages only 1.8 kWh, but for a few minutes hob, oven, kettle, dishwasher heater and heat pump run together: on 1 evening in 10 the power reaches 6.5 kW. Today's highest expected short peak: 7.1 kW around 08:00.
insights.tip: Stagger big loads: boil the kettle before the oven preheats, start the dishwasher after cooking (or by timer at night).

insights.title: The evening peak
insights.detail: 17:00–22:00 costs €0.40/kWh and is when the whole family is home (dinner, screens, heating): €1,310 of €3,202 a year.
insights.tip: Pre-heat before 17:00, start the dishwasher by timer after midnight, and use the oven before 17:00 on weekends.

household.name: Marek & Ania
household.title: A Silesian Family Home
household.description: Family of four in an older detached house in Katowice with a heat pump. Marek works rotating shifts, Ania works hybrid, Kuba and Zosia go to school.

items: Marek works a 3-shift rota that rotates every week: morning (06–14, away 06–15), afternoon (14–22, away 14–23), night (22–06, away 22–07, sleeps 07–14). Mon–Fri, plus a Saturday shift on 1 in 4 weekends.
Ania works from home every Tuesday and Thursday and on 25% of the other weekdays; office days she is away 08–17.
Kuba (14) is at school 08–15 and Zosia (10) 08–14 on school days. Kuba has football Mon/Wed 16–18, Zosia dance Tue/Fri 16–18.
School breaks: 22–31 Dec, 2–15 Feb (Silesian winter break), 2–7 Apr (Easter), 27 Jun–31 Aug. Polish public holidays incl. 24 Dec (new since 2025).
Unplanned events the forecast cannot know: weekend family outings (35% of weekend days, 3–6 h), evenings out, sick days, occasional weekend trips.
Power and energy per use are drawn uniformly from the ranges in the brief (e.g. kettle 2 kW × 3–5 min, hob 1.5–3.5 kW).
Cooking follows meals: breakfast at each person's wake-up time, lunch when an adult is home, kids' snack after school, dinner 17:30–19:30 (± 45 min), and a late meal after Marek's shift.
Screens run only when their users are at home and awake; Ania's laptop runs through her home-office hours.
Washing machine ≈ 4.5 cycles/week, dishwasher ≈ 6 cycles/week, both started only when an adult is home.
Lighting is on when people are awake at home and the real solar radiation is below 20 W/m² (dark).
Air-to-water heat pump; older house heat loss 0.25 kW per °C (thermal). COP falls from 3.6 at 7 °C to 2.4 at −7 °C.

Setpoints 21 °C day, 19.5 °C night (22–06), 20 °C when nobody is home; heating fades out as the average outdoor temperature of the last 24 hours rises from 13 °C (full heating) to 17 °C (off), like a weather-compensated heat pump in spring and autumn.
Electric power 1.5–3.5 kW while running (brief); a smaller need means the heat pump cycles on and off within the hour.
Internal gains 80 W per person at home; solar gains from real radiation. No domestic hot water in the heat pump (not in the brief).
Real hourly weather for Katowice (50.26 °N, 19.02 °E) from Open-Meteo: archive for the history, forecast API for the next 7 days.
The historical profile is simulated hour by hour from the schedules above and the real weather, 1 Oct 2025 → yesterday (≈ 1 year, well above the 30-day minimum).
Times are local (Europe/Warsaw); on daylight-saving changes the missing or doubled hour is interpolated so every day has 24 hours.
HackoWatt common tariff €0.18 / €0.28 / €0.40 / €0.28 per kWh; export €0.08/kWh; PV €1,300 per kWp; PV running cost 1% of the investment per year.

PV production from JRC PVGIS for Katowice: south-facing, 35° tilt, 14% system loss, 2019–2023 hourly average → 1,072 kWh per kWp per year. Next-days PV from the Open-Meteo radiation forecast on the same tilted plane.
Payback = investment ÷ (yearly bill saving + export income − 1% running cost). Scenario B also moves the washing machine and dishwasher to the best hour of their window.
The forecast knows the planned calendar (shifts, home-office days, school, holidays) and the weather forecast — not the unplanned events.

8 models (incl. LSTM and GRU neural networks) are compared on 8 test weeks (winter, spring and the 4 latest weeks), each trained only on the data before its week; the most accurate one is used. It is calibrated so that at most 1 in 5 days is under-predicted, and a likely range (10–90 %) is shown.

Online learning: when smart-meter readings are available, every complete day is added to the history, the model is re-trained on all data and the calibration is refreshed (update_model.py). No real meter is connected in this demo.
The optimiser only moves the washing machine, the dishwasher and heat-pump timing (pre-heating the house before the €0.40 peak); comfort stays inside the chosen band.

household.name: Marek & Ania
household.title: A Silesian Family Home
household.description: Family of four in an older detached house in Katowice with a heat pump. Marek works rotating shifts, Ania works hybrid, Kuba and Zosia go to school.

items: Marek works a 3-shift rota that rotates every week: morning (06–14, away 06–15), afternoon (14–22, away 14–23), night (22–06, away 22–07, sleeps 07–14). Mon–Fri, plus a Saturday shift on 1 in 4 weekends.
Ania works from home every Tuesday and Thursday and on 25% of the other weekdays; office days she is away 08–17.
Kuba (14) is at school 08–15 and Zosia (10) 08–14 on school days. Kuba has football Mon/Wed 16–18, Zosia dance Tue/Fri 16–18.
School breaks: 22–31 Dec, 2–15 Feb (Silesian winter break), 2–7 Apr (Easter), 27 Jun–31 Aug. Polish public holidays incl. 24 Dec (new since 2025).
Unplanned events the forecast cannot know: weekend family outings (35% of weekend days, 3–6 h), evenings out, sick days, occasional weekend trips.
Power and energy per use are drawn uniformly from the ranges in the brief (e.g. kettle 2 kW × 3–5 min, hob 1.5–3.5 kW).
Cooking follows meals: breakfast at each person's wake-up time, lunch when an adult is home, kids' snack after school, dinner 17:30–19:30 (± 45 min), and a late meal after Marek's shift.
Screens run only when their users are at home and awake; Ania's laptop runs through her home-office hours.
Washing machine ≈ 4.5 cycles/week, dishwasher ≈ 6 cycles/week, both started only when an adult is home.
Lighting is on when people are awake at home and the real solar radiation is below 20 W/m² (dark).
Air-to-water heat pump; older house heat loss 0.25 kW per °C (thermal). COP falls from 3.6 at 7 °C to 2.4 at −7 °C.

Setpoints 21 °C day, 19.5 °C night (22–06), 20 °C when nobody is home; heating fades out as the average outdoor temperature of the last 24 hours rises from 13 °C (full heating) to 17 °C (off), like a weather-compensated heat pump in spring and autumn.
Electric power 1.5–3.5 kW while running (brief); a smaller need means the heat pump cycles on and off within the hour.
Internal gains 80 W per person at home; solar gains from real radiation. No domestic hot water in the heat pump (not in the brief).
Real hourly weather for Katowice (50.26 °N, 19.02 °E) from Open-Meteo: archive for the history, forecast API for the next 7 days.
The historical profile is simulated hour by hour from the schedules above and the real weather, 1 Oct 2025 → yesterday (≈ 1 year, well above the 30-day minimum).
Times are local (Europe/Warsaw); on daylight-saving changes the missing or doubled hour is interpolated so every day has 24 hours.
HackoWatt common tariff €0.18 / €0.28 / €0.40 / €0.28 per kWh; export €0.08/kWh; PV €1,300 per kWp; PV running cost 1% of the investment per year.

PV production from JRC PVGIS for Katowice: south-facing, 35° tilt, 14% system loss, 2019–2023 hourly average → 1,072 kWh per kWp per year. Next-days PV from the Open-Meteo radiation forecast on the same tilted plane.
Payback = investment ÷ (yearly bill saving + export income − 1% running cost). Scenario B also moves the washing machine and dishwasher to the best hour of their window.
The forecast knows the planned calendar (shifts, home-office days, school, holidays) and the weather forecast — not the unplanned events.

8 models (incl. LSTM and GRU neural networks) are compared on 8 test weeks (winter, spring and the 4 latest weeks), each trained only on the data before its week; the most accurate one is used. It is calibrated so that at most 1 in 5 days is under-predicted, and a likely range (10–90 %) is shown.

Online learning: when smart-meter readings are available, every complete day is added to the history, the model is re-trained on all data and the calibration is refreshed (update_model.py). No real meter is connected in this demo.
The optimiser only moves the washing machine, the dishwasher and heat-pump timing (pre-heating the house before the €0.40 peak); comfort stays inside the chosen band.

insights.title: Heating is your biggest cost
insights.detail: 6,661 kWh of your 10,663 kWh a year goes to heating (≈ €1,865 of €3,202).
insights.tip: Small changes to heating matter more than anything else in the house.

insights.title: Every degree colder costs you
insights.detail: Each 1 °C drop in outdoor temperature adds about 2.5 kWh of heating per day (≈ €0.69).
insights.tip: Lowering the indoor setpoint by 1 °C saves roughly the same as a 1 °C warmer day.

insights.title: Today is a high-demand day
insights.detail: 18.4 kWh forecast vs 13.2 kWh on an average past day with similar weather (56 days at 14–18 °C). Heating today 5.6 kWh vs 2.6 kWh on those days — coldest hour 11.1 °C.
insights.tip: Follow today's actions: the plan pays off most on high-demand days.

insights.title: Your daily peak
insights.detail: Appliances add 1.42 kWh at 18:00 and 1.45 kWh at 19:00 on top of heating, at €0.40/kWh.
insights.tip: Avoid starting flexible appliances in these hours.

insights.title: The oven is a big occasional load
insights.detail: On days it is used it takes 1.9 kWh — 346 kWh a year (≈ €136).
insights.tip: Oven dinners in the 17–22 peak cost 43% more than before 17:00 — batch-cook at the weekend or use residual heat.

insights.title: Washing machine timing
insights.detail: 235 cycles a year (187 kWh), most often at 06:00. Running every cycle at the cheapest allowed hour saves about €28 a year.
insights.tip: Best price: €0.18/kWh (the cheapest hours of the day).

insights.title: Dishwasher timing
insights.detail: 309 cycles a year (312 kWh), most often at 20:00. Running every cycle at the cheapest allowed hour saves about €69 a year.
insights.tip: Best price: €0.18/kWh (the cheapest hours of the day).

insights.title: Heat-ahead over a year
insights.detail: Today's plan saves €0.20 on 6 kWh of heating. Applied to your 6,661 kWh of yearly heating that is roughly €239 (estimate).
insights.tip: Needs a heat-pump controller or smart thermostat that can follow a schedule.

insights.title: Always-on devices
insights.detail: Refrigerator, Wi-Fi router, Standby devices use 920 kWh a year, around the clock.
insights.tip: A switchable power strip removes part of the standby load.

insights.title: Marek's shift weeks
insights.detail: Without heating, weekdays in afternoon-shift weeks use 11.2 kWh and in morning-shift weeks 10.6 kWh (morning 10.6, afternoon 11.2, night 10.9). The forecast knows the rota in advance.
insights.tip: In night-shift weeks Marek sleeps 7–14 — quiet appliances (dishwasher, washer) are better started in the evening window or by timer.

insights.title: Ania's home-office days
insights.detail: Home-office weekdays use 11.2 kWh vs 10.7 kWh on office days (laptop, lunch cooking, kettle, lighting) — plus the house stays heated to 21 °C instead of 20 °C.
insights.tip: On home-office days, cook lunch and run the washing machine in the solar/cheaper midday hours instead of the evening.

insights.title: Short power peaks
insights.detail: In the evening the hour averages only 1.8 kWh, but for a few minutes hob, oven, kettle, dishwasher heater and heat pump run together: on 1 evening in 10 the power reaches 6.5 kW. Today's highest expected short peak: 7.1 kW around 08:00.
insights.tip: Stagger big loads: boil the kettle before the oven preheats, start the dishwasher after cooking (or by timer at night).

insights.title: The evening peak
insights.detail: 17:00–22:00 costs €0.40/kWh and is when the whole family is home (dinner, screens, heating): €1,310 of €3,202 a year.
insights.tip: Pre-heat before 17:00, start the dishwasher by timer after midnight, and use the oven before 17:00 on weekends.

household.name: Marek & Ania
household.title: A Silesian Family Home
household.description: Family of four in an older detached house in Katowice with a heat pump. Marek works rotating shifts, Ania works hybrid, Kuba and Zosia go to school.

items: Marek works a 3-shift rota that rotates every week: morning (06–14, away 06–15), afternoon (14–22, away 14–23), night (22–06, away 22–07, sleeps 07–14). Mon–Fri, plus a Saturday shift on 1 in 4 weekends.
Ania works from home every Tuesday and Thursday and on 25% of the other weekdays; office days she is away 08–17.
Kuba (14) is at school 08–15 and Zosia (10) 08–14 on school days. Kuba has football Mon/Wed 16–18, Zosia dance Tue/Fri 16–18.
School breaks: 22–31 Dec, 2–15 Feb (Silesian winter break), 2–7 Apr (Easter), 27 Jun–31 Aug. Polish public holidays incl. 24 Dec (new since 2025).
Unplanned events the forecast cannot know: weekend family outings (35% of weekend days, 3–6 h), evenings out, sick days, occasional weekend trips.
Power and energy per use are drawn uniformly from the ranges in the brief (e.g. kettle 2 kW × 3–5 min, hob 1.5–3.5 kW).
Cooking follows meals: breakfast at each person's wake-up time, lunch when an adult is home, kids' snack after school, dinner 17:30–19:30 (± 45 min), and a late meal after Marek's shift.
Screens run only when their users are at home and awake; Ania's laptop runs through her home-office hours.
Washing machine ≈ 4.5 cycles/week, dishwasher ≈ 6 cycles/week, both started only when an adult is home.
Lighting is on when people are awake at home and the real solar radiation is below 20 W/m² (dark).
Air-to-water heat pump; older house heat loss 0.25 kW per °C (thermal). COP falls from 3.6 at 7 °C to 2.4 at −7 °C.

Setpoints 21 °C day, 19.5 °C night (22–06), 20 °C when nobody is home; heating fades out as the average outdoor temperature of the last 24 hours rises from 13 °C (full heating) to 17 °C (off), like a weather-compensated heat pump in spring and autumn.
Electric power 1.5–3.5 kW while running (brief); a smaller need means the heat pump cycles on and off within the hour.
Internal gains 80 W per person at home; solar gains from real radiation. No domestic hot water in the heat pump (not in the brief).
Real hourly weather for Katowice (50.26 °N, 19.02 °E) from Open-Meteo: archive for the history, forecast API for the next 7 days.
The historical profile is simulated hour by hour from the schedules above and the real weather, 1 Oct 2025 → yesterday (≈ 1 year, well above the 30-day minimum).
Times are local (Europe/Warsaw); on daylight-saving changes the missing or doubled hour is interpolated so every day has 24 hours.
HackoWatt common tariff €0.18 / €0.28 / €0.40 / €0.28 per kWh; export €0.08/kWh; PV €1,300 per kWp; PV running cost 1% of the investment per year.

PV production from JRC PVGIS for Katowice: south-facing, 35° tilt, 14% system loss, 2019–2023 hourly average → 1,072 kWh per kWp per year. Next-days PV from the Open-Meteo radiation forecast on the same tilted plane.
Payback = investment ÷ (yearly bill saving + export income − 1% running cost). Scenario B also moves the washing machine and dishwasher to the best hour of their window.
The forecast knows the planned calendar (shifts, home-office days, school, holidays) and the weather forecast — not the unplanned events.

8 models (incl. LSTM and GRU neural networks) are compared on 8 test weeks (winter, spring and the 4 latest weeks), each trained only on the data before its week; the most accurate one is used. It is calibrated so that at most 1 in 5 days is under-predicted, and a likely range (10–90 %) is shown.

Online learning: when smart-meter readings are available, every complete day is added to the history, the model is re-trained on all data and the calibration is refreshed (update_model.py). No real meter is connected in this demo.
The optimiser only moves the washing machine, the dishwasher and heat-pump timing (pre-heating the house before the €0.40 peak); comfort stays inside the chosen band.

household.name: Marek & Ania
household.title: A Silesian Family Home
household.description: Family of four in an older detached house in Katowice with a heat pump. Marek works rotating shifts, Ania works hybrid, Kuba and Zosia go to school.

items: Marek works a 3-shift rota that rotates every week: morning (06–14, away 06–15), afternoon (14–22, away 14–23), night (22–06, away 22–07, sleeps 07–14). Mon–Fri, plus a Saturday shift on 1 in 4 weekends.
Ania works from home every Tuesday and Thursday and on 25% of the other weekdays; office days she is away 08–17.
Kuba (14) is at school 08–15 and Zosia (10) 08–14 on school days. Kuba has football Mon/Wed 16–18, Zosia dance Tue/Fri 16–18.
School breaks: 22–31 Dec, 2–15 Feb (Silesian winter break), 2–7 Apr (Easter), 27 Jun–31 Aug. Polish public holidays incl. 24 Dec (new since 2025).
Unplanned events the forecast cannot know: weekend family outings (35% of weekend days, 3–6 h), evenings out, sick days, occasional weekend trips.
Power and energy per use are drawn uniformly from the ranges in the brief (e.g. kettle 2 kW × 3–5 min, hob 1.5–3.5 kW).
Cooking follows meals: breakfast at each person's wake-up time, lunch when an adult is home, kids' snack after school, dinner 17:30–19:30 (± 45 min), and a late meal after Marek's shift.
Screens run only when their users are at home and awake; Ania's laptop runs through her home-office hours.
Washing machine ≈ 4.5 cycles/week, dishwasher ≈ 6 cycles/week, both started only when an adult is home.
Lighting is on when people are awake at home and the real solar radiation is below 20 W/m² (dark).
Air-to-water heat pump; older house heat loss 0.25 kW per °C (thermal). COP falls from 3.6 at 7 °C to 2.4 at −7 °C.

Setpoints 21 °C day, 19.5 °C night (22–06), 20 °C when nobody is home; heating fades out as the average outdoor temperature of the last 24 hours rises from 13 °C (full heating) to 17 °C (off), like a weather-compensated heat pump in spring and autumn.
Electric power 1.5–3.5 kW while running (brief); a smaller need means the heat pump cycles on and off within the hour.
Internal gains 80 W per person at home; solar gains from real radiation. No domestic hot water in the heat pump (not in the brief).
Real hourly weather for Katowice (50.26 °N, 19.02 °E) from Open-Meteo: archive for the history, forecast API for the next 7 days.
The historical profile is simulated hour by hour from the schedules above and the real weather, 1 Oct 2025 → yesterday (≈ 1 year, well above the 30-day minimum).
Times are local (Europe/Warsaw); on daylight-saving changes the missing or doubled hour is interpolated so every day has 24 hours.
HackoWatt common tariff €0.18 / €0.28 / €0.40 / €0.28 per kWh; export €0.08/kWh; PV €1,300 per kWp; PV running cost 1% of the investment per year.

PV production from JRC PVGIS for Katowice: south-facing, 35° tilt, 14% system loss, 2019–2023 hourly average → 1,072 kWh per kWp per year. Next-days PV from the Open-Meteo radiation forecast on the same tilted plane.
Payback = investment ÷ (yearly bill saving + export income − 1% running cost). Scenario B also moves the washing machine and dishwasher to the best hour of their window.
The forecast knows the planned calendar (shifts, home-office days, school, holidays) and the weather forecast — not the unplanned events.

8 models (incl. LSTM and GRU neural networks) are compared on 8 test weeks (winter, spring and the 4 latest weeks), each trained only on the data before its week; the most accurate one is used. It is calibrated so that at most 1 in 5 days is under-predicted, and a likely range (10–90 %) is shown.

Online learning: when smart-meter readings are available, every complete day is added to the history, the model is re-trained on all data and the calibration is refreshed (update_model.py). No real meter is connected in this demo.
The optimiser only moves the washing machine, the dishwasher and heat-pump timing (pre-heating the house before the €0.40 peak); comfort stays inside the chosen band.

insights.title: Heating is your biggest cost
insights.detail: 6,661 kWh of your 10,663 kWh a year goes to heating (≈ €1,865 of €3,202).
insights.tip: Small changes to heating matter more than anything else in the house.

insights.title: Every degree colder costs you
insights.detail: Each 1 °C drop in outdoor temperature adds about 2.5 kWh of heating per day (≈ €0.69).
insights.tip: Lowering the indoor setpoint by 1 °C saves roughly the same as a 1 °C warmer day.

insights.title: Today is a high-demand day
insights.detail: 18.4 kWh forecast vs 13.2 kWh on an average past day with similar weather (56 days at 14–18 °C). Heating today 5.6 kWh vs 2.6 kWh on those days — coldest hour 11.1 °C.
insights.tip: Follow today's actions: the plan pays off most on high-demand days.

insights.title: Your daily peak
insights.detail: Appliances add 1.42 kWh at 18:00 and 1.45 kWh at 19:00 on top of heating, at €0.40/kWh.
insights.tip: Avoid starting flexible appliances in these hours.

insights.title: The oven is a big occasional load
insights.detail: On days it is used it takes 1.9 kWh — 346 kWh a year (≈ €136).
insights.tip: Oven dinners in the 17–22 peak cost 43% more than before 17:00 — batch-cook at the weekend or use residual heat.

insights.title: Washing machine timing
insights.detail: 235 cycles a year (187 kWh), most often at 06:00. Running every cycle at the cheapest allowed hour saves about €28 a year.
insights.tip: Best price: €0.18/kWh (the cheapest hours of the day).

insights.title: Dishwasher timing
insights.detail: 309 cycles a year (312 kWh), most often at 20:00. Running every cycle at the cheapest allowed hour saves about €69 a year.
insights.tip: Best price: €0.18/kWh (the cheapest hours of the day).

insights.title: Heat-ahead over a year
insights.detail: Today's plan saves €0.10 on 6 kWh of heating. Applied to your 6,661 kWh of yearly heating that is roughly €119 (estimate).
insights.tip: Needs a heat-pump controller or smart thermostat that can follow a schedule.

insights.title: Always-on devices
insights.detail: Refrigerator, Wi-Fi router, Standby devices use 920 kWh a year, around the clock.
insights.tip: A switchable power strip removes part of the standby load.

insights.title: Marek's shift weeks
insights.detail: Without heating, weekdays in afternoon-shift weeks use 11.2 kWh and in morning-shift weeks 10.6 kWh (morning 10.6, afternoon 11.2, night 10.9). The forecast knows the rota in advance.
insights.tip: In night-shift weeks Marek sleeps 7–14 — quiet appliances (dishwasher, washer) are better started in the evening window or by timer.

insights.title: Ania's home-office days
insights.detail: Home-office weekdays use 11.2 kWh vs 10.7 kWh on office days (laptop, lunch cooking, kettle, lighting) — plus the house stays heated to 21 °C instead of 20 °C.
insights.tip: On home-office days, cook lunch and run the washing machine in the solar/cheaper midday hours instead of the evening.

insights.title: Short power peaks
insights.detail: In the evening the hour averages only 1.8 kWh, but for a few minutes hob, oven, kettle, dishwasher heater and heat pump run together: on 1 evening in 10 the power reaches 6.5 kW. Today's highest expected short peak: 7.1 kW around 08:00.
insights.tip: Stagger big loads: boil the kettle before the oven preheats, start the dishwasher after cooking (or by timer at night).

insights.title: The evening peak
insights.detail: 17:00–22:00 costs €0.40/kWh and is when the whole family is home (dinner, screens, heating): €1,310 of €3,202 a year.
insights.tip: Pre-heat before 17:00, start the dishwasher by timer after midnight, and use the oven before 17:00 on weekends.
